note: Window agent p1790-p1799 (Phase D, 2 Nov 2026). Entries: Luxembourg and Loon gaps at the end of 1795, South Prussia colony land of 1793, Qajar Khorasan 1796, and rulings for the left bank of the Rhine 1795-1799. events/keyframe_overrides/rulings keep their order.

region.text: the Duchy of Luxembourg, annexed with the Southern Netherlands

events.note: 1 October 1795: Luxembourg is annexed. The Siege of Luxembourg page: 'On 1 October 1795, most of Luxembourg became part of the Departement des Forets' (created 24 October 1795), after the capitulation of 7 June 1795. The ledger's Belgium gain leaves the duchy unowned at the end of 1795 (habsburg-netherlands dissolves in October with Luxembourg in its region); France holds it from 1796.

union.text: the county of Loon, approximately the Belgian province of Limburg

region.text: the principality's land outside Liège province: Loon (Belgian Limburg) and Horne

events.note: 1795: the whole principality is annexed. The Prince-Bishopric of Liège page: 'The role of the bishop as prince permanently ended when the state was annexed by France in 1795.' The ledger's gain names Liège province only, so the county of Loon (about 10 cells) and Horne are nobody's at the end of 1795 and French only from the 1796 keyframe.

region.text: South Prussia of 1793: the Poznań, Kalisz and Gniezno voivodeships of Greater Poland (south of the Netze District), the lands of Sieradz and Łęczyca, the Kuyavian voivodeship of Brześć and Dobrzyń Land, and adjacent parts of the Płock and Rawa voivodeships; without Thorn (West Prussia) and the Lesser Poland land south of the Pilica

events.note: 25 September 1793: South Prussia is created. The page: 'was a province of the Kingdom of Prussia from 1793 to 1807', 'created out of territory annexed in the Second Partition of Poland' ('2nd Polish Partition: 25 September 1793'), capital Poznan. Prussia's own January 1793 gain already holds the land, so the found event moves only 16 cells and the colony's other 181 cells stay Prussia's direct land until the 1795 keyframe.

region.text: the lands of Dobrzyń and Płock northeast of the Vistula

events.note: 1795: the lands of Dobrzyn and Plock go to New East Prussia. South Prussia page: 'the lands of Dobrzyn and Plock northeast of the Vistula river were transferred to New East Prussia' after the Third Partition. With South Prussia now holding its 1793 land (events/2), the 7 Plock cells that Prussia's own 1793 gain holds as direct land are no longer reached by the ledger's gain from south-prussia, and the snap threshold no longer fires; this gain from kingdom-of-prussia moves them.

minus.text: Persian Baluchistan: Khash, Bampur, Qasr-e Qand, Zahedan and the Iranian Makran coast, held by the Khanate of Kalat

union.text: Cliopatria's Qajar shape of 1796 without Persian Baluchistan (Khash, Bampur, Qasr-e Qand, Zahedan and the Iranian Makran coast), which the Khanate of Kalat held until the early 19th century
Mashhad and Khorasan, entered on 14 May 1796

correction.text: Cliopatria's Qajar shape of 1796 without Persian Baluchistan (as the dossier has it), plus all of Razavi Khorasan: Mashhad was entered on 14 May 1796

keyframe_overrides.why: The page: Agha Mohammad Khan 'entered Mashhad on 14 May' and 'A year after Agha Mohammad Khan re-subjugated the Caucasus [1795], he also captured Khorasan'; crowned 1796. The Cliopatria shape of 1796 holds only half of Khorasan, so the keyframe snap strips the 241 Razavi Khorasan cells the ledger gave in May 1796 (qajar-dynasty ledger/9) and leaves them nobody's at the end of 1796; the 1797 keyframe adds them back.

union.text: Minnesota east of the Mississippi: the province-of-quebec_1774 polygon less the land west of the river (the p1770-p1779 rulings/0 polygon of Minnesota west of the Mississippi, and the Leech Lake pocket inside the river's upper loop between Lake Itasca, Grand Rapids and Aitkin)
the whole of Wisconsin up to the Mississippi (the dossier's 1791-1809 corrections cut off its western cells at 92 W)
the whole of Kentucky (Cliopatria's shapes leave holes)

correction.text: the treaty land east of the Mississippi that the 1791-1809 corrections leave unowned: Minnesota east of the river, western Wisconsin and the Kentucky holes

keyframe_overrides.why: New keyframe, unioned with the alive US keyframes of 1791-1809 (the same repair p1780-p1789 keyframe_overrides/0-1 made for the shapes of 1783 and 1788, which every later shape repeats). Article 2 of the Treaty of Paris, as the page quotes it: the line runs through the Great Lakes to the Lake of the Woods, 'to the northwesternmost point thereof, and from thence on a due west course to the river Mississippi' and then 'along the middle of the said river'; the page adds that the Mississippi does not extend so far north, so that line never meets it. Everything east of the river up to that line is the United States'. Against the current dossiers the US shape of 1791 is the 1788 shape without the repair: its snap sets 394 US cells to nobody (Minnesota east of the river 289, Wisconsin 43, Georgia 35, Kentucky 26, one more); the Spanish Empire's own 1792 shape then takes the 288 Minnesota cells (1792-1799), French Louisiana takes all of the east bank in 1800 (1800-1803) and the US has it only from 1804. This keyframe restores Minnesota east of the Mississippi, western Wisconsin and the Kentucky holes. It does not restore the 35 cells of southern Georgia that the p1780-p1789 overrides gave the United States: the Article 2 line is the 31st parallel and the page does not place Georgia south of it. The Louisiana Purchase shapes of 1805-1809 repeat the Wisconsin and Kentucky gaps. Runs to 1821, not 1810: the Cliopatria shapes of 1811-1821 still omit the Wisconsin and Kentucky cells (the draft has Wisconsin's 43 cells ownerless until 1821 and Kentucky's 3 until 1819), so ending at 1810 would drop the cells back to nobody in 1811; the p1820-p1829 overrides of united-states-of-america_1822 restore them from 1822.

region.text: the left bank of the Rhine, as the French dossier's occupation (french-directory ledger/2)

rulings.why: Peace of Basel (5 April 1795): Prussia 'recognised the French control of the west bank of the Rhine' pending a cession by the Imperial Diet; the French dossier (ledger/2) models the left bank as an occupation until Campo Formio. The size rule gave this state's left-bank land to itself as plain direct land; it stays the state's, drawn occupied by France. Corrected by the reviewer (2 Nov 2026): limited to the left bank, because without a region the ruling's only conflict cell was the bishopric's right-bank land by Ladenburg (cell centred 8.55E 49.43N, east of the Rhine), which it drew French-occupied in 1796, while the same page says 'France returned all of the lands east of the Rhine captured during the war'.

Treaty of Campo Formio (17 October 1797): the secret clauses 'agreed to the extension of the borders of France up to the Rhine, the Nette, and the Roer'; the French dossier books the left bank as a gain in October 1797 (ledger/10). The size rule kept it with the smaller German state.

region.text: the 49-50.3 N band of north-western Ontario that Rupert's Land held up to 1782 (Lac Seul, the Lake Nipigon country and the Albany headwaters)

rulings.why: Continues p1780-p1789 rulings/1 (Quebec against Rupert's Land, 1783-1789) for Quebec's western successor. Upper Canada's found and keyframe of December 1791 overlap Rupert's Land over the 266 cells of north-western Ontario between 49 N and 50.3 N, and R1 gave them to Upper Canada as the smaller colony; they were Rupert's Land's through 1790. The Province of Quebec page: the Quebec Act took Quebec 'north to the southern boundary of lands owned by the Hudson's Bay Company, or Rupert's Land'; the Constitutional Act 'divided the colony in two at the Ottawa River', and the page is silent on any boundary between the new colonies and Rupert's Land after 1791 (the Upper Canada page says only that the act 'did not yet specify official borders'), so the line stays where it was and Rupert's Land keeps the band. The ruling runs to Upper Canada's end (February 1841) because the dossier's later keyframes (upper-canada_1812, _1813, _1815) use the same 'Upper Canada' gazetteer region and would take the band from Rupert's Land again in 1812 (a 266-cell jump with no event behind it); it acts only in years when the two conflict. The Upper Canada page, opened for this, names no northern boundary and no change of one before 1841: 'The act divided the province of Quebec into Upper and Lower Canada, but did not yet specify official borders', and Canada West's boundaries were afterwards 'identical to those of the former province of Upper Canada'.

region.text: Minnesota: the stray cell of the East India Company shape in the Arrowhead (48.0 N, 90.2 W)

rulings.why: Continues the stray-cell cut of p1780-p1789 keyframe_overrides/3, which covers the 1788 shape (1788-1790) only: Cliopatria's East India Company shapes of 1791, 1792, 1794, 1796, 1797, 1799, 1800 and 1803-1809 all draw the same cell in the Minnesota Arrowhead, and the size rule gives it to the Company (about 0.5-1.6 M km2) over the United States (1.1 M km2 and more) wherever the keyframes meet it. The East India Company page names no territory in North America: its only North American mention is the tea trade of 1773, and the Company 'gained control of large parts of the Indian subcontinent and Saint Helena'. The cell is the United States', as the Treaty of Paris line puts the Arrowhead in the United States.
